title: Chapter 3. Padas of Radha's Mood: Navadvipa, Sannyasa, Puri
html:
Narahari Sarakara's Navadvipa padas in which the Lord experiences Radha's mood (in the Padakalpataru they stand as gaura-chandrikas to the sections on purvaraga, vasakasajja, vipralabdha and khandita) and which Majumdar (Sri-Chaitanya-chariter upadan, ch. 2) regards as descriptions of real moods seen by an eyewitness; padas by Ananta and Gauridasa on Gaura and Nitai, on the sannyasa and on Nityananda's "market"; then Puri and Navadvipa in the years of separation: Sarvabhauma, the waiting for the Lord and a dream of His return, Radha's mood in the company of Svarupa, the divine madness of prema. The text follows the Padakalpataru (PK), the Bhakti-ratnakara (BR), the Kshanada-gita-chintamani (KGC) and the Gaura-pada-tarangini (GPT1 — 1st ed., 1903; GPT2 — 2nd ed., 1934); the Bengali original, variants and word-for-word translation are in the full version of the book.

1. Narahari (Sarakara) — "gaurāṅga ṭhekila pāke…" (PK 2122; BR, p. 924)

Lila: Navadvipa — the Lord in Krishna's mood: the Ganga seems to Him the Yamuna, a flowering garden — Vrindavana; He asks for yellow cloth and a flute and embraces Gadadhara. According to Majumdar — an eyewitness's pada (1509). Raga mallar (PK, KGC, GPT), ashavari (BR).1

গৌরাঙ্গ ঠেকিল পাকে ।
ভাবের আবেশে রাধা রাধা বলি ডাকে ॥ ধ্রু ॥

gaurāṅga ṭhekila pāke |
bhābera ābeśe rādhā rādhā bali ḍāke || dhru ||

gauranga — Gauranga; thekila pake — was caught in a whirlpool (a noose); bhabera abeshe — absorbed in bhava; radha radha boli dake — calls "Radha, Radha!"

1.1(Refrain) Gauranga is caught in a whirlpool:
absorbed in bhava, He calls, "Radha, Radha!"2

সুরধুনী দেখি পহু যমুনার ভানে ।
ফুল-বন দেখি বৃন্দাবন পড়ে মনে ॥

suradhunī dekhi pahu yamunāra bhāne |
phula-bana dekhi bṛndābana paṛe mane ||

suradhuni dekhi — seeing the Suradhuni (the Ganga); pahu — the Lord; yamunara bhane — takes it for the Yamuna; phula-bana dekhi — seeing a flower garden; vrindavana pare mane — remembers Vrindavana

1.2Seeing the Suradhuni, the Lord takes it for the Yamuna;
seeing a flowering garden, He remembers Vrindavana.

পূরব-আবেশেতে তিরিভঙ্গ হয়ে ।
পীত বসন আর মুরলী চাহয়ে ॥

pūraba-ābeśete tiribhaṅga haye |
pīta basana āra muralī cāhaye ||

puraba-abeshete — in the mood of [His] former [lila]; tiribhanga haye — bending in three places; pita basana — yellow cloth; ara murali — and the flute; chahaye — asks for

1.3In the mood of His former lila He stands bent in three places
and asks for yellow cloth and a flute.3

প্রিয় গদাধর পহু করিয়া ত কোলে ।
কোথা ছিলা কোথা ছিলা গদগদ বোলে ॥

priya gadādhara pahu kariyā ta kole |
kothā chilā kothā chilā gadagada bole ||

priya gadadhara — the beloved Gadadhara; pahu — the Lord; kariya ta kole — taking into His embrace; kotha chhila kotha chhila — "where were you? where were you?"; gadagada bole — says in a faltering voice

1.4Taking His beloved Gadadhara into His embrace,
the Lord says in a faltering voice, "Where were you? Where were you?"

ভাব বুঝি পণ্ডিত রহে বাম পাশে ।
না বুঝয়ে এহ রঙ্গ নরহরি দাসে ॥

bhāba bujhi paṇḍita rahe bāma pāśe |
nā bujhaye eha raṅga narahari dāse ||

bhaba bujhi — understanding the mood; pandita — the Pandita (Gadadhara); rahe bama pashe — stays at the left side; na bujhaye — does not fathom; eha ranga — this play; narahari dase — Narahari Dasa

1.5Understanding His mood, the Pandita stays at His left.
Narahari Dasa does not fathom this play.4

of Sri Narahari Sarakara Thakura" — the only pada signed "Narahari" in BR that he expressly ascribes to Sarakara, and Majumdar puts it first among Narahari's Navadvipa padas. It is also found in KGC (27th kshanada, as a gaura-chandrika) and in GPT1 (p. 280, no. 9); in PK it stands in the section "The form of Sri Gauranga, etc." In BR it is preceded by the words: "By this road Gora goes to the bank of the Suradhuni… He calls, 'Radha, Radha!'" Cf. CC Antya 18: in Puri the sea seems to the Lord to be the Yamuna. the Ganga. Vrindavana lila. Here the Lord is in Krishna's mood, while Gadadhara Pandita, according to the Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika (vv. 147–153), is a manifestation of Radha in Gaura's lila. KGC and GPT read simply "taking into His embrace", BR — "clasping Gadadhara to His breast". The humble "does not fathom" in the signature is Narahari's usual formula.

2. Narahari (Sarakara) — "mo mena manu gorācāndere dekhiyā…" (PK 103)

Lila: Navadvipa — Gaura walks along the road to the Ganga; a young townswoman tells how she saw Him. In PK — a gaura-chandrika to purvaraga (love dawning at first sight). According to Majumdar — Narahari Sarakara's pada about a real mood, though it contains expressions of nagari-bhava. Raga dhanashi.5

মো মেন মনু গোরাচান্দেরে দেখিয়া ।
অপরূপ রূপ কাচা কাঞ্চন জিনিয়া ॥

mo mena manu gorācāndere dekhiyā |
aparūpa rūpa kācā kāñcana jiniyā ||

mo — I; mena (mene) manu — as if died (?); gorachandere dekhiya — seeing Gorachand; aparupa rupa — a wondrous form; kancha kanchana jiniya — surpassing pure (unworked) gold

2.1Seeing Gorachand, I all but died:6
wondrous is His form — it outshines pure gold.

খেনে শীঘ্রগতি চলে মারে মালসাট ।
খেনে থির হৈয়া চলে সুরধুনী-বাট ॥

khene śīghragati cale māre mālasāṭa |
khene thira haiyā cale suradhunī-bāṭa ||

khene — now; shighra-gati chale — walks swiftly; mare malsat — slaps His shoulders (like a wrestler); khene thira haiya — now, grown calm; chale suradhuni-bat — walks along the road to the Suradhuni

2.2Now He walks swiftly, slapping His shoulders like a wrestler,
now, grown calm, He steps slowly along the road to the Suradhuni.7

অরুণ নয়ানে ঘন চাহে অনিবার ।
হানিলে নয়ান-বাণ হিয়ার মাঝার ॥

aruṇa nayāne ghana cāhe anibāra |
hānile nayāna-bāṇa hiyāra mājhāra ||

aruna nayane — with reddish eyes; ghana chahe anibara — gazes again and again, unceasingly; hanile nayana-bana — shot the arrows of His glances; hiyara majhara — into the midst of the heart

2.3With His reddish eyes He gazes again and again, unblinking —
and has driven the arrows of His glances into the very heart.

আজানুলম্বিত ভুজ দোলে দুই দিগে ।
যুবতি যৌবন দিতে চাহে অনুরাগে ॥

ājānulambita bhuja dole dui dige |
yubati yaubana dite cāhe anurāge ||

ajanulambita bhuja — arms reaching to the knees; dole dui dige — sway on both sides; yubati — young women; yaubana dite chahe — long to give [their] youth; anurage — in love

2.4His arms, reaching to the knees, sway on either side;
young women, in love, long to give Him their youth.8

খেনে মন্দ মন্দ হাসি খেনে উতরোল ।
না বুঝিয়া নরহরি হইল বিভোর ॥

khene manda manda hāsi khene utarola |
nā bujhiyā narahari haila bibhora ||

khene manda manda hasi — now smiling softly; khene utarola — now in loud joy; na bujhiya — not understanding; narahari haila bibhora — Narahari became lost in rapture

2.5Now He smiles softly, now He shouts for joy;
not fathoming it, Narahari is lost in rapture.

transition" (after a pada by Radhamohana); in GPT1 — p. 170, no. 41 (raga dhanashi). Majumdar discusses it among the nine Navadvipa padas of Narahari Sarakara in PK and cites the line "With His reddish eyes He gazes again and again". "manu" — an old form for "I died" (cf. "malum̐"); "I think I perished" is also possible. The sense is the shock of seeing Gaura. Lord does the same in kirtana ("now He slaps His shoulders, now calls 'Krishna!', now 'Radha!'"). The Suradhuni is the Ganga. townswomen); we translate them faithfully to the author. Vrindavana Dasa stresses that in this incarnation the Lord never looked at another man's wife; the Gaudiya tradition (Vrindavana Dasa, Krishnadasa Kaviraja, Bhaktisiddhanta) does not accept the worship of Gaura in the spirit of "gaura-nagari". In PK the pada is a gaura-chandrika: it sets the tone for Radha's purvaraga, and the attraction here is an image of prema for Krishna, not of a worldly feeling.

3. Narahari (Sarakara) — "ki lāgiyā mora gaura-sundara…" (PK 307)

Lila: Navadvipa — the Lord in the mood of Radha as vasakasajja (the heroine who adorns herself and the bower while awaiting her beloved) dresses Himself and waits for Krishna. In PK — a gaura-chandrika to "vasakasajja in spring". According to Majumdar — a description of a real mood; the Lord's dress and ornaments in the Navadvipa padas are not invented. Raga dhanashi.9

কি লাগিয়া মোর গৌর-সুন্দর
বসিয়া গৃহের মাঝে ।
বসন আসন রতন-ভূষণ
সাজয়ে অঙ্গের মাঝে ॥

ki lāgiyā mora gaura-sundara
basiyā gṛhera mājhe |
basana āsana ratana-bhūṣaṇa
sājaye aṅgera mājhe ||

ki lagiya — why; mora gaura-sundara — my beautiful Gaura; basiya grihera majhe — sitting in the house; basana asana — clothes, seat; ratana-bhushana — jewelled ornaments; sajaye angera majhe — arranges on His body

3.1Why does my beautiful Gaura
sit in the house
and, preparing clothes, a seat and jewelled ornaments,
adorn His body with them?

আপন বপুর ছাহ হেরিয়া
চমকি উঠয়ে মনে ।
কি লাগি অবহুঁ না মিলল পহুঁ
এত না বিলম্ব কেনে ॥

āpana bapura chāha heriyā
camaki uṭhaye mane |
ki lāgi abahum̐ nā milala pahum̐
eta nā bilamba kene ||

apana bapura chhaha heriya — seeing the shadow of His own body; chamaki uthaye mane — starts in His heart; ki lagi — why; abahun na milala pahun — has the Lord not come even now; eta na bilamba kene — why such delay

3.2Seeing the shadow of His own body,
He starts in His heart:
"Why has the Lord not come even now?
Why does He delay so long?"10

কহে নরহরি মোর গৌরহরি
ভাবিয়া রাইয়ের দশা ।
সজল নয়ানে চাহে পথ পানে
কহে গদ গদ ভাষা ॥

kahe narahari mora gaurahari
bhābiyā rāiyera daśā |
sajala nayāne cāhe patha pāne
kahe gada gada bhāṣā ||

kahe narahari — Narahari says; mora gaurahari — my Gaurahari; bhabiya raiyera dasha — thinking of Rai's condition; sajala nayane — with tearful eyes; chahe patha pane — looks at the road; kahe gada gada bhasha — speaks in a faltering voice

3.3Narahari says: my Gaurahari,
thinking of Rai's condition,
looks at the road with tear-filled eyes
and speaks in a faltering voice.

the pada as an example that Narahari's gaura-chandrikas are not conventional preludes but descriptions of moods he saw; that the Lord wore ornaments in Navadvipa is attested by the sannyasa pada PK 2241 (chapter 2, no. 5): "golden armlets… — all that enchanting attire He gave up." rustle, thinking Krishna has come. The Lord experiences Her waiting; this is a manifestation of prema, not of worldly longing.

4. Narahari (Sarakara) — "hema darapaṇi gaurāṅga-lābaṇi…" (PK 316)

Lila: Navadvipa — the Lord in the mood of Radha as vipralabdha (the deceived heroine whose beloved did not come to the tryst) rolls in the dust, calls "Lord of My life!" and weeps before His companions. In PK — a gaura-chandrika to "vipralabdha in spring". According to Majumdar — a pada of vipralambha (separation). Raga bhairavi.11

হেম দরপণি গৌরাঙ্গ-লাবণি
ধূলায় ধূসর কাঁতি ।
আসন বসন তেজিয়া রোদন
ব্রজ-বিলাসিনী ভাঁতি ॥

hema darapaṇi gaurāṅga-lābaṇi
dhūlāya dhūsara kām̐ti |
āsana basana tejiyā rodana
braja-bilāsinī bhām̐ti ||

hema darapani — a golden mirror; gauranga-labani — Gauranga's beauty; dhulaya dhusara kanti — the lustre grey with dust; asana basana tejiya — leaving seat and clothes; rodana — weeping; braja-bilasini bhanti — like a beauty of Vraja

4.1Gauranga's beauty is like a golden mirror,
yet its lustre is grey with dust;
leaving His seat and clothes, He weeps
like a beauty of Vraja.

হরি হরি বলি প্রাণনাথ করি
ধরণী ধরিয়া উঠে ।
কোথা না যাইব কাহারে কহিব
পরাণ ফাটিয়া উঠে ॥

hari hari bali prāṇanātha kari
dharaṇī dhariyā uṭhe |
kothā nā yāiba kāhāre kahiba
parāṇa phāṭiyā uṭhe ||

hari hari boli — crying "Hari, Hari!"; prananatha kari — calling [Him] Lord of life; dharani dhariya uthe — rises holding the ground; kotha na yaiba — where shall I go; kahare kahiba — whom shall I tell; parana phatiya uthe — the heart is bursting

4.2Crying "Hari, Hari!", calling Him Lord of His life,
He rises, leaning on the ground:
"Where shall I go? Whom shall I tell?
My heart is breaking!"

সহচরগণে করিয়া রোদনে
কহয়ে বদন তুলি ।
আমার পরাণ করয়ে যেমন
বেদন কাহারে বলি ॥

sahacaragaṇe kariyā rodane
kahaye badana tuli |
āmāra parāṇa karaye yemana
bedana kāhāre bali ||

sahacharagane — to the companions; kariya rodane — weeping; kahaye badana tuli — speaks raising His face; amara parana karaye yemana — what my heart is going through; bedana kahare boli — to whom shall I tell the pain

4.3Weeping, He speaks to His companions,
raising His face:
"What is happening to My heart —
to whom can I tell this pain?"

নরহরি দাসে গদ গদ ভাষে
কহয়ে গৌরাঙ্গ মোর ।
আন ছলে বুলে উদ্ধারে সকলে
সদা রাধা-প্রেমে ভোর ॥

narahari dāse gada gada bhāṣe
kahaye gaurāṅga mora |
āna chale bule uddhāre sakale
sadā rādhā-preme bhora ||

narahari dase — Narahari Dasa; gada gada bhashe — in a faltering voice; kahaye — says; gauranga mora — my Gauranga; ana chhale bule — wanders under another pretext; uddhare sakale — delivers all; sada radha-preme bhora — ever drunk with Radha's love

4.4Narahari Dasa says in a faltering voice:
my Gauranga
wanders under another pretext, delivering all —
yet He Himself is ever drunk with Radha's love.12

the text because the other sections of this pallava open with gaura-chandrikas. In GPT1 (p. 307, no. 27) with minor variants. B. B. Majumdar (1961) gives the pada from a Baranagar manuscript with the reading "aśana basana" ("food and clothes") instead of "āsana basana" ("seat and clothes"). one — to taste Radha's love. Narahari expresses the same thought: delivering the world is the "pretext", while the Lord's heart is ever in Radha's prema.

5. Narahari (Sarakara) — "āre mora āre mora gaurāṅga rāya…" (PK 408)

Lila: Navadvipa — the Lord in the mood of Radha as khandita (the heroine whose beloved comes at dawn bearing the marks of a tryst with another) angrily reproaches Krishna. In PK — a gaura-chandrika to the section "Khandita — the impatient (adhira) madhya". According to Majumdar — Narahari Sarakara's pada of the khandita. Raga suhai.13

আরে মোর আরে মোর গৌরাঙ্গ রায় ।
পুরুব প্রেমভরে মৃদু চলি যায় ॥

āre mora āre mora gaurāṅga rāya |
puruba premabhare mṛdu cali yāya ||

are mora are mora — ah, my, ah, my; gauranga raya — Gauranga Raya; puruba prema-bhare — full of former love; mridu chali yaya — walks slowly

5.1Ah, my, ah, my Gauranga Raya!
Full of His former love, He walks with slow steps.

অরুণ নয়ন মুখ বিরস হইয়া ।
কোপে কহয়ে পহুঁ গদ-গদ হিয়া ॥

aruṇa nayana mukha birasa haiyā |
kope kahaye pahum̐ gada-gada hiyā ||

aruna nayana — eyes reddened; mukha birasa haiya — face darkened; kope kahaye pahun — in anger the Lord says; gada-gada hiya — His heart trembling (haltingly)

5.2His eyes have reddened, His face has darkened;
in anger, His heart trembling, the Lord speaks haltingly:

জানলুঁ তোহারে তোর কপট পিরীতি ।
যা সঞে বঞ্চিলা নিশি তাহা কর নতি ॥

jānalum̐ tohāre tora kapaṭa pirīti |
yā sañe bañcilā niśi tāhā kara nati ||

janalun tohare — I know You; tora kapata piriti — Your false love; ya sanne banchila nishi — with whom You spent the night; taha kara nati — to her bow down

5.3"I know You, I know Your false love!
Go and bow to her with whom You spent the night."14

এত কহি গৌরাঙ্গের গর-গর মন ।
ভাবের তরঙ্গে যেন নিশি-জাগরণ ॥

eta kahi gaurāṅgera gara-gara mana |
bhābera taraṅge yena niśi-jāgaraṇa ||

eta kahi — having said this; gaurangera gara-gara mana — Gauranga's mind is overwhelmed; bhabera tarange — in the waves of bhava; yena nishi-jagarana — as if after a night's vigil

5.4Having said this, Gauranga is wholly overcome by bhava:
in the waves of bhava He is as if after a sleepless night.

কহে নরহরি রাধার ভাবে হৈল হেন ।
পাই আশোয়াস বঞ্চিত হৈল যেন ॥

kahe narahari rādhāra bhābe haila hena |
pāi āśoyāsa bañcita haila yena ||

kahe narahari — Narahari says; radhara bhabe — in Radha's mood; haila hena — He became thus; pai ashoyasa — having received assurance; banchita haila yena — as if deceived

5.5Narahari says: in Radha's mood He has become
like one who was given a promise and deceived.

the line "I know You, I know Your false love". The khandita is one of the eight heroines of rasa-shastra (Ujjvala-nilamani). (mana) are a manifestation of the highest prema, not a worldly feeling; the Lord experiences them in Her mood.

6. Narahari (Sarakara) — "gorā pahum̐ birale basiyā…" (PK 421)

Lila: Navadvipa — the Lord in the mood of Radha as khandita sits alone after a sleepless night and weeps: "Having given Me hope, You deceived Me all night." In PK — a gaura-chandrika to "khandita — the composed-impatient (dhira-adhira) madhya". According to Majumdar — Narahari Sarakara's pada of the khandita. Raga gandhara.15

গোরা পহুঁ বিরলে বসিয়া ।
অবনত বদন করিয়া ॥

gorā pahum̐ birale basiyā |
abanata badana kariyā ||

gora pahun — Lord Gora; birale basiya — sitting alone; abanata badana kariya — lowering His face

6.1Lord Gora, sitting alone,
has lowered His face.

ভাবাবেশে ঢুলু ঢুলু আঁখি ।
রজনি জাগিল হেন সাখি ॥

bhābābeśe ḍhulu ḍhulu ām̐khi |
rajani jāgila hena sākhi ||

bhababeshe — in bhava; dhulu dhulu ankhi — eyes drooping; rajani jagila — kept awake all night; hena sakhi — such is the witness

6.2In bhava His eyes are heavy with sleep —
the sleepless night is witness to it.

বিরস-বদনে কহে বাণী ।
আশা দিয়া বঞ্চিল রজনী ॥

birasa-badane kahe bāṇī |
āśā diyā bañcila rajanī ||

birasa-badane — with a faded face; kahe bani — speaks words; asha diya — having given hope; banchila rajani — [You] deceived [me] all night

6.3With a faded face He says:
"Having given Me hope, You deceived Me all night."

কান্দিয়া কহয়ে গোরা রায় ।
এ দুখ সহনে নাহি যায় ॥

kāndiyā kahaye gorā rāya |
e dukha sahane nāhi yāya ||

আপাদ-মস্তক প্রেম-ধারা বরিখত
চৌদিগে ঝলকত কিরণে ।

চাঁদ উদয় করু চরণে ॥

yemana temana kule — in whatever family; janama hauka mora — may I be born; yemana temana deha paiya — receiving whatever body; ananta dasera mana — Ananta Dasa's wish; thakura gaurangera guna — Thakura Gauranga's qualities; deshe deshe phiri — wandering from land to land; yena gaiya — that [I may] sing

of the Lord; PK has 32 padas with his signature. In GPT1 (p. 39, no. 41) and GPT2 with variants. and GPT "Gaurangachand" (cām̐dere ye): "…fashioned Gaurangachand, taking on his own body". Praise of Gaura and Nitai — the two brothers who purify the fallen: They give prema to all without distinction and weep on seeing the fallen. দেখ দেখ অপরূপ গৌরাঙ্গ নিতাই ।
অখিল জীবের ভাগ্যে অবনী বিহরে গো

By the good fortune of all living beings there wander the earth

প্রেম-অমৃত করি পানে ॥

uttama adhama nāhi māne |

prema-amṛta kari pāne ||

yare dekhe — whomever They see; tara thame — to him; yachiya bilaya preme — entreating, They distribute prema; uttama adhama nahi mane — make no distinction of high and low; e tina bhubanera loka — the people of the three worlds; nahi jara mrityu shoka — no old age, death or sorrow; prema-amrita kari pane — having drunk the nectar of prema

kare kamaṇḍalu daṇḍa dharilā gaurāṅgacandra
